drivers.text: Google Cloud revenue growth came mainly from Google Cloud Platform (infrastructure and platform services) and TPU system sales; management also cites enterprise AI infrastructure and AI solutions demand.
Google Cloud operating income rose on higher revenue, partly offset by inventory and related costs from TPU system sales and technical infrastructure usage costs.
Cost of revenues up 24%, driven by TPU-system inventory costs, depreciation expense, TAC and YouTube content costs.
Capex of $51.4 billion in the quarter mainly reflects technical infrastructure investment; Alphabet-level activities (shared AI R&D) swung to a larger loss of 7,655 vs 4,467.
Alphabet raised cash via senior unsecured notes (net $28.7 billion), ATM share issuance and June 2026 equity and mandatory convertible preferred offerings, to fund AI infrastructure capex.

gaps: capex_guidance: no dollar capex guidance in the release or 10-Q; only the qualitative statement that 2026 technical-infrastructure investment will significantly increase versus 2025.
rpo_next_12m_pct: not disclosed; the 10-Q gives just over 55% over the next 24 months.
da_q is depreciation of property and equipment only; no combined depreciation and amortization line was found in the release cash flow statement.

useful_life_change: no change in server useful life found in the 10-K or Q3 10-Q text; the 10-K says servers and network equipment are depreciated generally over six years and that any change is applied prospectively.

capex_incl_finance_leases_q: no single disclosed figure; inputs are purchases of PP&E 51,355, finance-lease assets obtained 2,085 and financing cash flows used for finance leases 1,110. Also 159 million (Q3) of lease prepayments for leases not yet commenced (10-Q line 869).
Quote for the Q3 2026 headcount on the release line carries both years; the 10-Q MD&A (line 1789) also states 204,757.
